paper_title: New solar X-ray constraints on keV Axion-Like Particles
suggested_experiment_name: Solar X-ray trapped ALP (SphinX + NuSTAR, Coalescence)
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, as plotted on y-axis
notes: Astrophysical (solar X-ray) constraint on keV ALPs from decay of gravitationally trapped ALPs, using SphinX and NuSTAR data. Main result is the coalescence-production exclusion limit in the (g_agamma, m) plane (Fig. 1), valid ~3-40 keV, explicitly NOT relying on any local DM density assumption. Data points are approximate readings of the strongest (coalescence) exclusion curve from Fig. 1; exact tabulated values not provided in paper. Paper also discusses g_ae (Compton) but the primary published limit is on g_agamma. | [VISION GATE D] vision notes admit tracing a compilation envelope ('envelope of the blue 'Coalescence' curves') rather than the paper's own single curve | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0.6, 31)) | Vision: Traced the lower envelope of the blue 'Coalescence' curves (NuSTAR solid + SphinX dashed) in Fig. 1, the paper's headline hadronic-axion (g_ae=0) exclusion in the (g_agamma, m) plane. This is the strongest/lowest boundary; the excluded region lies above it. X-axis log scale 3-40 keV with only '10' explicitly labeled; masses interpolated on log scale and converted keV->eV. Y-axis matches provided calibration (1e-13 to 1e-9). The minimum of ~4e-13 occurs near 12 keV. Fig. 4 shows an alternative version with g_ae variation but with a different y-range (1e-15 to 1e-10); I used Fig. 1 per calibration.
